verdict.rationale: Stripe's main cross-merchant discovery path, ACS for agents, does let an AI interface 'discover products' with product feed ingestion. But it is private preview and requires a seller-initiated OCA agreement, which contradicts the 'no private partnership' condition. The self-service paths are thin: a single mention of a Link CLI guide to 'Search products and complete payments with UCP' (CLI on public npm), and Stripe Directory for finding external service providers. Missing for 10: documented self-service or keyless product search across merchants outside the private-preview, OCA-gated ACS; depth on the Link CLI/UCP search flow; independent or hands-on corroboration of search working without partnership.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, my agent can programmatically search products or services across merchants — keylessly or with self-service credentials, no private partnership required

citations.quote: ACS works across multiple commerce protocols, so your AI interface can discover products, collect payment information, and complete purchases on behalf of sellers.
Search products and complete payments with UCP
Stripe Directory helps developers and AI agents find the best external providers for a task and follow the best supported path to provision or use them.
An OCA is a required connection between your agent and a seller that enables agentic commerce flows. Only a seller can initiate an OCA request
